correctness.rationale: For fixed W, JR iff every candidate has fewer than q unrepresented supporters. Distinct equal-sized members of a laminar support family are disjoint; each quota class must therefore contribute an elected candidate. Consequently all valid DR committees cover the same U, and feasibility is exactly the residual test plus M>=k (r<=floor(n/q)<=k). Counting independent nonempty selections from classes gives [z^k] product_i((1+z)^w_i-1). Stirling proves the sampling asymptotic. Exact comparison to independently enumerated committees passed 134760 finite tests; none is used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Natural exact classification of an emerging voting axiom on hierarchical support families. The result gives a full existence criterion and count in polynomial time, an invariant represented population across all feasible committees, and an exact exponentially small uniform-sampling success probability on a motivated family. This contrasts with general DR decision hardness and improves actionable interpretation of quota-exact diversity beyond one-off examples. The overlap counterexample delineates structural scope.
